title: URL-resolution conformance case
description: One resolution. A base, an input, and either the exact string returned or the exact refusal — reason and message both, so two bindings are held to the same words and not merely to the same verdict.

base.description: The base URL. Deliberately unconstrained: one case supplies a base that is not a URL at all, which is what invalid-base pins.

input.description: The path-or-URL being resolved. Unconstrained for the same reason — most cases assert a malformed value is refused.

url.description: On success: the exact string returned. Never a normalised form — §4 concatenates and §5 returns the input unchanged.

message.description: On refusal: the exact §7 message. A binding that refuses for the right reason with different words fails the case, which is the point — the message is contract text.
